claims.text: The premelting and melting behavior of Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by their chemical complexity.
The premelting and melting behavior of Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by nanoscale size effects.
Chemical complexity and nanoscale size alter the thermodynamic properties of these nanoparticles relative to bulk alloys or single-metal nanoparticles.
Chemical complexity and nanoscale size alter the kinetic properties of these nanoparticles relative to bulk alloys or single-metal nanoparticles.
The Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are initially solid.
A controlled atmosphere can prevent oxidation or other chemical reactions during heating.
The nanoparticles will exhibit premelting and melting behavior distinct from that of bulk Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu alloys.
The nanoparticles will exhibit premelting and melting behavior distinct from that of single-metal nanoparticles.
The Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles may have lower melting points than the proposed baselines.
The Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles may undergo more gradual phase transitions than the proposed baselines.
The proposed hypothesis is intended to apply to particles 1–100 nm in size.
The proposed hypothesis is intended to apply over 500–1500 K.
Indistinguishable melting behavior relative to single-metal nanoparticles or bulk alloys would falsify the hypothesis.
